correctness.rationale: For a squarefree binary form of degree p in characteristic p, the Jacobian criterion identifies singularities with zeros of df. At such a zero, squarefreeness forces a first nonconstant exponent 2<=m<=p-1; extracting an m-th root of the local unit gives v^p=u^m. The semigroup <p,m> has delta (p-1)(m-1)/2. Since df is a nonzero section of O(p-2), the critical multiplicities sum to p-2, so the total delta is the arithmetic genus. The characteristic-five example is checked by the included script; the general result follows from the proof, not from computation.

value.rationale: The family is used to construct strongly isotrivial elliptic surfaces in positive characteristic. An exact critical-divisor formula gives a reusable way to locate every cusp, determine its semigroup and delta invariant, and account for the full genus defect, rather than merely recovering a total arithmetic genus. The explicit characteristic-five example exhibits two distinct free-point cusp types in one such curve.
